events.statement: The only deployment across ALL services in the window 11:30-13:59Z is market-data-service v5.2.0, 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf', deployed at 11:56:00Z by v.rao, status live, rolled_back_at null (never rolled back). No deployment exists for pricing-engine or order-service.

The only config/flag change in the window is in pricing-engine: cfg-3120 key 'flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct' changed 5 -> 100 at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z by pm-experiments ('Ramp Greeks v2 experiment to all traffic'). Its timestamp is the exact same bucket/minute as the p99 latency jump (F1) and the CPU jump (F3), and matches the GreeksV2 calculator in pricing-engine's errors (F4).
No config changes were found for order-service or redis-cache in 11:30-13:59Z (both counts 0), so no timeout/pool/TLS/DNS/resource-limit change is recorded for the callee chain or the shared cache.

Dependency graph for order-service: it calls ledger-db (db, SHARED), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and produces to kafka (SHARED); api-gateway calls order-service. pricing-engine in turn calls market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache, SHARED). Shared components in the blast radius are ledger-db, redis-cache and kafka.

Historical precedent: HIST-113 (2026-01-28) 'pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open' has symptoms 'quote timeouts' and 'cpu 99%' on pricing-engine, category capacity_saturation, root cause 'Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity'. This is the same symptom pair as the current p99 2.6s / ~98-99.5% CPU picture, but its stated cause (organic volume) differs from a flag ramp.

Second relevant precedent is HIST-101 (auth-service, v6.4.0): a config-like change inside a release (bcrypt cost 10->14) produced high CPU + p99/503s and was resolved by rolling back the release; HIST-107 shows the shared redis-cache can cause quote latency via a cold-cache storm. Both are leads only, not evidence of the current cause.
